Justified text no longer stretches a line that ends a paragraph, an imported page survives binding data, and the
native library now says what the command line says: the warnings from laying a document out, and the same checks.

**Documents change if they use justified text or import a page.** Justified paragraphs with a line break, or long
enough to cross a page, come out with different spacing on those lines. A template that imports a page and is bound to
data now draws the page, where it was missing. A subset made with `hinting` off loses a few bytes per glyph. Nothing else
changes in the documents, and nothing was removed or renamed. Two native entry points and one drawing method are added,
hence 0.11 rather than 0.10.1.

## Fixed: justified text stretched the wrong lines

The backends drew every line of a justified text stretched but the last, with no way to tell a line the layout wrapped
from one the author ended. Three things came of that:

- **a line ended with a line break was stretched across the page**, "Short first line." pulled to the margin;
- **rich text did the same**, which is everything the content editor writes, since Enter goes to a new line there. The
  editor's own sheet never stretched such a line, so the screen and the PDF disagreed;
- **the last line on a page of a paragraph that goes on overleaf was left ragged**, in every long justified document.

A line that ends a paragraph is now never stretched, and every line the layout wrapped is, the last one on a page
included.

- **The `sound.justifiedBreak` rule is gone**: it reported the first fault, for plain text only.
- **The designer's preview now justifies rich text.** It drew it left-aligned, under a note saying Justify did nothing,
  and the note is gone.
- **A text placed at coordinates with a width**, and holding `{Pages}`, no longer loses its line breaks when the total
  is filled in.

## Fixed: an imported page went missing once data was bound

Binding copies the template, and the page read from the other PDF was not part of the copy. Every page read before
binding, which is the order the command line uses, reached the layout unread and drew nothing, with exit code 0. Bound
copies now keep what was read.

A page imported onto the back page was never read at all, bound or not. It is now read and drawn.

A page that nothing has read is now reported. `fits.importedPageUnread` names it, once per page. Through the native
library, which has no PDF reader, that is every imported page.

## Fixed: a subset without hinting carried stale padding

With `hinting` off, a subset kept the padding the font had aligned each glyph with, and padded again: up to four excess
bytes per glyph, which fontTools reports. A glyph now ends where its points end. Nothing is drawn differently.

## New in the native library

| Entry point | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fk_render_issues` | the warnings from laying out the document `fk_render` returned: a page limit passed, something taller than a page, an imported page nobody read |
| `fk_template_check_for` | what `frisket check` checks: a misspelt property in the text, what the output being made cannot carry, which of your fields the template names wrongly, and what the data brings that cannot be drawn |

`fk_template_check_for` takes `fk_render`'s options, plus `"accessible"` and `"fields"` (your field catalogue). Both
functions write the same JSON as `frisket check --json`: `{ rule, level, message, where, pointer }`. The `pointer` is a
JSON Pointer into the template.

`fk_template_check` keeps its question, the template alone, and now writes that same JSON, `pointer` included. The C++,
Pascal and Python wrappers carry both new entry points.

## New for hosts embedding the content editor

`release/frisket-editor-element.standalone.js`, in the repository, is `<frisket-editor>` in one file:

- it holds the four scripts and the two stylesheets, and fetches nothing else;
- only the tag is added to the page, so a host's own `t` or `esc` is left alone;
- the four parts can still be loaded as before.

Two fixes in the editor:

- **the editor that ships gives a document 2 mm margins**, and the drag handles, a table's row buttons and its
  add-column button sat in that margin, off the sheet. You could not drag a block or add a row, and a horizontal
  scrollbar appeared. The sheet now leaves them room beside the paper;
- **the designer** names a new report in the interface's language.

## Worth checking

- **Justified documents differ**, on the lines described above. A host comparing documents byte for byte will see it.
- **`sound.justifiedBreak` is no longer reported.** A host that filters findings on it can drop the filter.
- **`fk_template_check` adds a `pointer`** and writes `message` before `where`. A reader that takes keys by name is
  unaffected.
- **A custom drawing surface** implementing `IReportBackend` keeps working unchanged. To stretch the right lines it
  implements the new `DrawText` overload that takes `endsParagraph`. `PlacedItem.ParagraphEnds` carries the same flags
  for a renderer of its own.
